chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, who said:
I heard Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام saying:

Concerning a man who killed his wife intentionally, he said: “If her family wishes to kill him, they shall return to his family half of the diyah. And if they wish, they may take half of the diyah, five thousand dirhams.”
And he said regarding a woman who killed her husband intentionally: “If his family wishes to kill her, they may kill her, and no one bears more than the consequence of his own crime against himself.”

key_terms.أَهْلُهَا: her family; the legal heirs entitled to claim qisas or diyah
key_terms.أَهْلُهُ: his family; the legal heirs entitled to claim retaliation
key_terms.خَمْسَةَ آلَافِ دِرْهَمٍ: five thousand dirhams; the specified amount of half the diyah here
key_terms.نِصْفَ الدِّيَةِ: half of the blood money due in this legal circumstance
key_terms.يَجْنِي: commits an offense or incurs liability through a crime

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a husband or wife intentionally kills their spouse in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out legal rulings for intentional killing between spouses in cases of qisas. It explains the differing financial implications when a husband kills his wife versus when a wife kills her husband, and affirms that liability is attached to the perpetrator’s own act.
